teaser.text: Beauty is not one product business but a portfolio of brands that turns formulas, identity and distribution into repeat purchases. To understand The Estée Lauder Companies, follow the product from a shopper’s choice to the money that reaches ELC and then leaves again.

stock.title: ELC stock forecast
stock.meta_description: ELC stock forecast: weighted scenarios, recovery drivers, real free cash flow and today’s valuation.
stock.opening: ELC's weighted forecast is $76.11 in October 2027. It hinges on turning recovery into durable consumer demand and cash.
stock.closing: The full memo also covers ELC's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could ELC's shares be in each forecast year?

paragraphs.text: The forecast’s weighted path remains below today’s price through the third forecast date. It is $76.11 in October 2027, a -27% return with dividends. It rises to $87.02 in October 2028, still a -15% return. By October 2029, it reaches $97.12, or -4% with dividends.
Today’s price is $105.50. The October 2029 outcomes span $27.25 to $202.59. The bear case has a 30% probability. The base case has a 55% probability. The bull case has a 15% probability.

blocks.heading: What could drive ELC's base, bear and bull cases?

paragraphs.text: The bear case carries 30% probability, the base case 55%. The bull case carries 15%. The base case requires earnings and valuation to recover. The bear case turns on weak China and travel-retail sell-through, discounting and stalled savings. The bull case needs launches and savings to support repeat demand.

blocks.heading: How much cash does ELC really make?

paragraphs.text: Capital spending fell from $1,040 million in fiscal 2022 to $457 million in fiscal 2026. That helps free cash flow, but factories, counters and digital systems still need investment. Subtracting $310 million of stock-based compensation produces an analytical “real free cash flow” of $1,006 million, because shares issued to employees dilute existing owners even without using operating cash.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for ELC today?

paragraphs.text: The trailing and forward P/E tell very different stories. P/E means the share price divided by earnings per share: trailing P/E uses the last twelve months, while forward P/E uses an estimate. Estée Lauder’s 215.3× trailing P/E reflects unusually weak recent profit, while its 26.8× forward P/E assumes a much stronger future. Management’s fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS guidance implies a different multiple, because the listed forward measure uses another period or adjustment policy.

blocks.heading: How much does ELC pay shareholders over time?

paragraphs.text: The dividend was $1.40 per share in fiscal 2026, down from $2.64 in fiscal 2024. ELC paid $508 million in dividends and also paid $300 million of deferred TOM FORD acquisition consideration. Cash therefore has to fund shareholders, brands, debt and restructuring at once.

blocks.heading: What is ELC's dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: Estée Lauder Companies (The) owns beauty brands including Clinique, M·A·C and La Mer, but its shares now depend on a substantial recovery in profit. At $105.50 on October 19, 2026, shareholders value the company at $38,225.05 million.

Free cash flow is more tangible than accounting profit, but it is not the same as the dividend. Fiscal 2026 operating cash flow less capital expenditure left about $1.316 billion, while dividends used $508 million. The difference can repay debt, support reinvestment or remain in reserve. The table shows the price and the main valuation measures an investor is paying for today.

earnings.title: ELC earnings
earnings.meta_description: ELC reports next on November 2, 2026; guidance calls for 3%–5% organic sales growth and adjusted EPS of $3.10–$3.35.
earnings.opening: ELC’s next results are expected on November 2, 2026. Watch whether stronger shipments reach shoppers and produce cash.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers how ELC’s business works, who its rivals are, how management operates, and what risks shape its recovery.

blocks.heading: What has ELC guided for fiscal 2027?

paragraphs.text: For fiscal 2027, management guides to 3%–5% organic sales growth. Adjusted EPS is guided to $3.10–$3.35. Adjusted operating margin is guided to 12.7%–13.5%. The plan targets $1.2 billion of annual gross benefits and a net reduction of 10,000 positions. It also carries more than $1.7 billion of cumulative restructuring and other charges.

The Profit Recovery and Growth Plan aims to deliver $1,200 million of annual gross benefits during fiscal 2027, alongside $1,700 million of cumulative restructuring and other charges and a net reduction of 10,000 positions. Gross benefits are savings before reinvestment and other pressures. ELC had accrued $632 million of restructuring costs at June 30, 2026, with expected cash payments of $530 million in fiscal 2027.

blocks.heading: What do ELC’s last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: The June 2026 quarter confirmed stronger sales, but still produced a reported loss.

The reported operating loss narrowed to $39 million from $390 million. Net loss narrowed to $116 million, while diluted EPS remained negative at $0.32. Restructuring and associated effects cost $306 million pretax, so the loss still reflected a large transformation bill.
